**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user is studying International Business.
- [FACT] The user has some experience in marketing and writing.
- [FACT] The user’s monthly income is around $2,500 AUD from a scholarship.
- [CHANGE] The user transferred all funds from their old bank account back home to a new Australian bank account on April 1st.
- [PREFERENCE] The user is concerned about overspending on food while getting used to prices in Melbourne.
- [EVENT] The user plans to start updating their resume and LinkedIn profile.
- [EVENT] The user is considering looking for job opportunities on campus.
- [PREFERENCE] The user thinks freelancing or online tutoring could be a good fit for them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant congratulated the user on taking the first step towards getting their finances in order.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested categorizing expenses into Essential Expenses (Needs) and Non-Essential Expenses (Wants).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of Essential Expenses, including rent, utilities, food, transportation, insurance, minimum debt repayment, and phone/internet.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of Non-Essential Expenses, including entertainment, savings, personal care, gifts, and miscellaneous expenses.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommended allocating 50-60% of income to Essential Expenses, 30-40% to Non-Essential Expenses, and 10-20% to Savings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested tracking expenses for a month using budgeting apps like Mint or You Need a Budget (YNAB).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for saving money on groceries, including meal planning, shopping at affordable supermarkets, buying in bulk, and using cashback apps.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for saving money on dining out, including cooking at home, looking for deals, and packing lunch.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested that the user consider a part-time job to supplement their scholarship income.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant calculated that with a part-time job paying $15-20 AUD per hour for 12 hours a week, the user could earn an additional $720-960 AUD per month.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised the user to check their scholarship terms regarding part-time work and to set realistic expectations for hours worked.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant discussed the pros and cons of freelancing and online tutoring as options for the user.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned platforms for freelancing, such as Upwork, Fiverr, and Freelancer.
